Nyirderzs Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírderzs, Hungary

Not demolished. Nyírderzs's Jewish cemetery is dated by its oldest tombstone to 1892, with its latest dated 1983. The village's Jewish population stood at 105 (of 607 residents) in 1880, later declining to 86 by 1910, 57 by 1930, and 69 by 1941. Notable residents included Sándor Fisch, a landowner and county committee member, and Jenő Kandel, a farmer trained at the Talmud School in Bratislava who managed a manorial farm before becoming independent in 1911. By 1945, no Jews remained in the village, and its former prayer room (shtiebel) has since been demolished.
